title: A Microfluidic-based Hydrodynamic Trap for Single Particles
protocol: Clean two silicon wafers with acetone and isopropyl alcohol.
Dry wafers with nitrogen gas.
Place wafers on a hotplate at 65°C for 1 minute.
Spin coat wafer #1 with SU-8 photoresist for 30 seconds at 4000 rpm to create a mold for the fluidic layer.
Spin coat wafer #2 with photoresist for 30 seconds at 1500 rpm to create a mold for the control layer.
Soft bake wafer #1 at 65°C for 3 minutes and then at 95°C for 6 minutes.
Soft bake wafer #2 at 65°C for 5 minutes and then at 95°C for 20 minutes.
Expose wafers to UV light with respective masks.
Post bake wafer #1 at 65°C for 1 minute and then at 95°C for 6 minutes.
Post bake wafer #2 at 65°C for 5 minutes and then at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Develop wafers with propylene glycol methyl ether acetate until uncured photoresist is removed.
Rinse wafers with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry wafers with nitrogen gas.
Silanize the surface of the SU-8 molds by placing wafers in a desiccator under vacuum for ~10 min with trichlorosilane.
Mix and degas PDMS in base:crosslinker ratios of 15:1 for the fluidic layer and 5:1 for the control layer.
Spin coat the 15:1 PDMS mixture onto the fluidic layer mold for 30 sec at 750 rpm, then place the wafer into a Petri dish.
Pour the 5:1 PDMS mixture onto the control layer mold to a thickness of ~4 mm and bake wafers/PDMS for 30 min at 70°C.
Cut the PDMS replica from the Petri dish with a scalpel after cooling down to room temperature.
Hole punch an access port to the microchannel using a 21 gauge needle.
Place the PDMS replica with the control layer onto wafer #1 (spin-coated fluidic layer).
Carefully align and seal the control layer to the fluidic layer using a stereo microscope.
Remove all air pockets between the layers.
Bake at 70°C overnight to fully cure both layers.
Cool PDMS replica containing control and fluidic layers to room temperature.
Cut and peel the PDMS replica off the SU-8 mold using a scalpel.
Remove excess PDMS and separate each device unit with a razor blade.
Hole punch access ports to microchannels in the fluidic layer with a 21 gauge needle.
Clean a coverslip (No: 1.5, 24 x 45 mm) with acetone and IPA.
Treat both the coverslip and PDMS replica surfaces with oxygen plasma under 500 mTorr for 30 sec.
Bring the treated surfaces into contact to form an irreversible seal.
Bake devices overnight to increase bonding between PDMS layers and coverslip.
Place microfluidic device onto stage of an inverted microscope and secure it with stage clips.
Fill two gas-tight syringes separately with buffer and sample solutions.
Place filled syringes on a Harvard Apparatus Syringe pump (PHD 2000 Programmable).
Deliver buffer and sample solutions to the microfluidic device through a 1 ml and 250 μl syringe, respectively.
Establish the fluidic connections between the syringes and the microfluidic device.
Connect the syringes to 1/16" outer diameter x 0.020" inner diameter perfluoroalkoxy tubing using luer-lock adapters.
Connect one end of the PFA tubing to the inlet ports of the microfluidic device with 24 gauge metal tubing.
Place a T-valve between the sample syringe and the sample port on the microfluidic device for controlling sample delivery.
Establish fluidic connections for the outlet channels in the microfluidic device.
Connect each outlet channel to PFA tubing (1/16" OD x 0.020" ID) using 24 gauge metal tubing.
Ensure both outlet tubes are of equal length and submerged into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube filled with buffer solution.
Fill the on-chip valve with fluorinated carrier oil using a 3 mL luer-lock plastic syringe to prevent air leakage during operation.
Push air in the valve chamber through the PDMS membrane into the microchannel in the fluidic layer.
Remove air from the device as fluid flows through the outlet ports.
Connect a nitrogen tank to the pressure regulator using tubing with an OD of ¼" and an ID of 0.170".
Connect the pressure regulator to the microfluidic device using PFA tubing with an OD of 1/16" and an ID of 0.020", terminated with 24 gauge metal tubing.
Rinse fluidic connections and the microfluidic device with 0.5 mL of buffer solution at a flow rate between 2000-5000 μL/hr to remove air bubbles.
Reduce the flow rate to 50-100 μL/hr for particle trapping after rinsing out air bubbles from the system.
Run the custom-built LabVIEW code.
Position the trapping region at the center of the camera view using the microscope x-y translation stage.
Bring the trapping region into focus with the objective lens.
Optimize imaging conditions by adjusting the camera settings.
Choose a rectangular region of interest (ROI) within the camera's field of view.
Initialize the offset pressure applied to the on-chip valve.
Introduce a 100-200 μm wide constriction in one of the outlet channels for an offset pressure.
Set the constant off-set pressure between 0-12 psi depending on channel dimensions and valve specifications.
Initiate the feedback controller.
Adjust the proportional gain to optimize trap response.
Trap a particle using the LabVIEW code.
Shut off the sample flow to isolate the trapped particle in buffer solution, if desired.
Monitor the trapped particle continuously.
Maintain particle focus within the image plane manually or with an automated setup.
Slightly adjust the proportional gain as needed to ensure trap stability over time.
Implement a linear feedback control algorithm using custom LabVIEW code.
Capture images from a CCD camera.
Transmit an electric potential to a pressure regulator.
Modulate the position of an on-chip dynamic pneumatic valve.
Adjust the hydrodynamic flow rate in one outlet line.
Reposition the stagnation point.
Enable hydrodynamic trapping.
Acquire an image for a "target" particle using fluorescence microscopy with a 10x objective lens and CCD camera.
Determine the centroid position of the particle.
Fit the emission intensity profile to a point spread function (PSF).
Calculate the centroid position from the PSF.
Calculate the updated pressure for the on-chip dynamic valve using a feedback control algorithm with a proportional controller.
Record time elapsed, centroid (x,y) position of the trapped particle, and position of the trap center for every image captured during particle trapping.
Measure distance of the particle from the trap center.
Record pressure applied to the on-chip valve.
Capture movie of the trapped particle in AVI file format.
Trap fluorescent polystyrene beads of various sizes using a hydrodynamic trap.
Determine the trajectory of a trapped particle from centroid position data recorded by LabVIEW code during a trapping event.
Track and localize the trapped particle from the recorded movie file to determine its trajectory.
Release the trapped bead after initial confinement for 3 min, allowing it to escape along one of the outlet channels.
Record particle trajectories along the compressional flow axis (inlet channel direction).
Observe that particle trajectories along the compressional flow axis are similar to those along the extensional flow axis.
Generate a histogram of particle displacement from the trap center for trapped beads along the outlet channel directions.
Confine trapped particles within ±1 μm of the trap center using the feedback control algorithm.
